text.p: Evergreen Media Corp and Chancellor Broadcasting Co said Wednesday they completed the purchase of ten radio stations from Viacom Inc for $1.08 billion plus working capital.
The companies said they received U.S. Federal Communications Commission approval on June 27.
Meanwhile, an Evergreen/Chancellor spokesman said the merger of the two companies, announced last February, was expected to close as soon as the third quarter.

The companies signed a joint deal to buy the Viacom radio stations, with the deal announced the same day as their merger. As part of the Viacom deal, Evergreen purchased two stations in New York and four in Washington for about $595 million.
Chancellor bought two stations in Los Angeles, one in Chicago and one in Detroit for about $480 million.
To comply with FCC ownership limits, Evergreen and Chancellor are unloading three of the four stations in Washington, D.C. and the one in Detroit.

Scott Ginsburg, chief executive officer of the new Chancellor Media, said the Viacom deal "dramatically strengthens our presence in the country's top markets of Los Angeles, New York, Chicago and Washington."

Chancellor Media Corp, the nation's largest pure-play radio broadcasting company, is being formed by the merger of Evergreen and Chancellor Broadcasting, as well as the Viacom deal, and the acquisition of five radio stations from Pacific and Southern Co Inc, a unit of Gannett Co Inc.
After all the deals are completed, Chancellor will own and operate 98 stations in 21 of the nation's largest markets.
